samples.text:
The line graph show the number of international students who studied at universities in three countries, Country A, B and C, between 2005 and 2023.

Country A had the most international students in all years. In 2005 there were 180 thousand students and this number increased every year until 2017, when it was 340 thousand. In 2020 it fell to 300 thousand, but then it increased again to 385 thousand in 2023.

Country B had 120 thousand students in 2005. The number was nearly same until 2011 and then rose slightly to 140 thousand in 2017. After that it was decreased to 110 thousand in 2020 and increase to 150 thousand in 2023.

Country C was the lowest in 2005 with only 30 thousand students. But it grew very fast and in 2014 it had 140 thousand, which was more than Country B. In 2023 it reached 240 thousand.

Overall, all three countries had more international students at the end, and all of them had a fall in 2020. Country C increase the most.
samples.why: Relevant overview placed at the end · key features and the 2020 dip covered · repetitive phrasing · adequate linking · errors in agreement, passive use and article omission that do not block meaning.

samples.text:
The graph provides information about international student enrolments at universities in three countries, labelled A, B and C, from 2005 to 2023.

Overall, the number of overseas students increased in all three countries across the period, although each experienced a noticeable drop in 2020. Country A attracted the largest numbers throughout, while Country C showed by far the fastest growth.

Country A began with 180,000 international students in 2005, and this figure climbed steadily to 340,000 in 2017. Following a fall to 300,000 in 2020, enrolments recovered strongly to reach a peak of 385,000 in 2023, more than double the original number.

Country B, by contrast, saw relatively little change. Its enrolments hovered between 115,000 and 125,000 until 2014, then rose to 140,000 in 2017 before dipping to 110,000 in 2020. By the end of the period the figure was 150,000. Country C started from a very low base of 30,000, but its numbers grew rapidly and it overtook Country B in 2014 with 140,000 students. Despite a slight decline in 2020, it finished on 240,000, eight times it's figure in 2005.
samples.why: Clear overview of trends and the shared 2020 dip · key features well highlighted · effective paragraph grouping · good lexical range · largely accurate grammar with one minor slip.

samples.text:
The line graph charts the number of international students enrolled at universities in three countries (A, B and C) at three-year intervals between 2005 and 2023.

In general, all three countries ended the period with more overseas students than at the start, despite a simultaneous downturn in 2020. Country A was consistently the most popular destination, while Country C registered the most remarkable growth, eventually overtaking Country B by a wide margin.

Enrolments in Country A rose uninterrupted from 180,000 in 2005 to 340,000 in 2017. Although numbers fell back to 300,000 in 2020, they rebounded sharply to 385,000 in 2023, the highest figure on the graph.

Country B's enrolments, in contrast, were remarkably stable, fluctuating narrowly between 115,000 and 140,000 for most of the period. After slipping to a low of 110,000 in 2020, they recovered to 150,000 by 2023. Country C, meanwhile, grew from just 30,000 students in 2005 to 140,000 in 2014, at which point it surpassed Country B. Its upward trajectory was only briefly interrupted in 2020, and by 2023 it had reached 240,000, an eightfold increase over the period.
samples.why: Well-selected key features including the crossover and 2020 downturn · clear overview · accurate, selective figures · sophisticated, precise vocabulary · wide range of structures with no noticeable errors.
